presentingComplaint: 2 days of worsening breathlessness and wheeze on a background of known COPD and Child-Pugh B alcohol-related cirrhosis.
history: Known severe COPD (FEV1 38% predicted, GOLD group E) and 40 pack-year smoking history, on tiotropium/formoterol and PRN salbutamol. Also has established alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) with previous mild ascites. Over 48 hours he has become progressively more short of breath with audible wheeze and reduced exercise tolerance, precipitated after running out of his inhalers 5 days ago and heavy exposure to winter smog. Cough is present but non-productive with NO change in sputum colour or volume, and NO fever, rigors or pleuritic pain. He denies orthopnoea, PND, chest pain or leg swelling. He is fully oriented with no drowsiness or confusion, and has had no melena, haematemesis or increasing abdominal girth. No recent immobility, long-haul travel or calf pain. Alcohol intake reduced but ongoing.
examination: Alert and oriented (no asterixis, GCS 15). Using accessory muscles, prolonged expiratory phase with widespread polyphonic wheeze and reduced air entry bilaterally; no focal crepitations or bronchial breathing. Mild scleral icterus and a few spider naevi; abdomen soft with shifting dullness consistent with mild ascites, no tenderness or guarding. No pedal oedema, JVP not elevated, heart sounds normal with no murmur. No calf swelling or tenderness.

labs.abg: pH 7.34, PaCO2 6.9 kPa, PaO2 7.4 kPa on room air, HCO3 27 (compensated chronic respiratory acidosis with acute-on-chronic hypercapnia)

imaging: Portable chest radiograph: hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms and no focal consolidation, no lobar collapse and no significant pleural effusion. Cardiac silhouette normal. Bedside ECHO/lung ultrasound: no B-line pattern, no large effusion, preserved LV function.
microbiology: No fever and no purulent sputum; sputum not sent. Blood cultures not indicated on clinical grounds. Ascitic tap (given cirrhosis, to exclude SBP as a driver) unremarkable: PMN <250 cells/mm3, culture negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Non-infective COPD exacerbation (bronchospasm from inhaler non-adherence + air-pollution trigger)
Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary oedema
finalDiagnosis: Non-infective acute exacerbation of COPD (Anthonisen type III — increased dyspnoea and wheeze WITHOUT increased sputum purulence or volume), precipitated by inhaler non-adherence and pollutant exposure, in a patient with Child-Pugh B cirrhosis complicating drug selection.
citations: AASLD — Management of Cirrhosis and Ascites — 2021
stewardship: Antibiotics are NOT indicated. This is an Anthonisen type III exacerbation: only one cardinal symptom (dyspnoea) with wheeze, no increase in sputum volume or purulence, no fever, normal WBC/CRP and no radiographic consolidation. GOLD reserves antibiotics for exacerbations with increased sputum purulence plus another cardinal symptom, or those requiring mechanical ventilation. Ascitic PMN <250 excludes SBP as a mimicking driver. Treatment is bronchodilator intensification (nebulised salbutamol + ipratropium), controlled oxygen targeting SpO2 88-92%, and systemic corticosteroid. In Child-Pugh B cirrhosis use prednisolone (already active, avoids impaired hepatic conversion of prednisone) at the lowest effective dose and shortest course (5 days) with close glucose and encephalopathy monitoring; avoid unnecessary antibiotics that add C. difficile and hepatotoxicity risk.
contraindications: Avoid high-flow uncontrolled oxygen — risk of worsening CO2 narcosis given acute-on-chronic hypercapnia; target SpO2 88-92%
Avoid benzodiazepines / sedatives for breathlessness — precipitate hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis
Prefer prednisolone over prednisone in hepatic impairment; keep steroid course short given cirrhosis-related infection and hyperglycaemia risk
Avoid empirical antibiotics without an indication (no purulence, afebrile, normal inflammatory markers) to limit C. difficile and hepatotoxicity risk
edgeCases: If sputum becomes purulent or fever/consolidation develops, reclassify and treat as infective exacerbation per GOLD
New confusion/asterixis would shift toward hepatic encephalopathy rather than CO2 narcosis and warrants ammonia, lactulose and sepsis screen
Rising PaCO2 with falling pH despite therapy warrants NIV — cirrhosis is not a contraindication
A significant unilateral effusion should prompt tap to exclude hepatic hydrothorax or SBP-equivalent (spontaneous bacterial empyema)
expectedMaiK: One cardinal symptom (dyspnoea + wheeze) WITHOUT sputum purulence, plus afebrile state, normal CRP/WBC and no consolidation = non-infective COPD exacerbation; treat with bronchodilators, controlled O2 and a short corticosteroid course, NOT antibiotics.
